claim: Junction Mapper is an open access, semi-automated software that defines the status of adhesiveness via the simultaneous measurement of pre-defined parameters at cell–cell contacts.
source: We designed Junction Mapper as an open access, semi-automated software that defines the status of adhesiveness via the simultaneous measurement of pre-defined parameters at cell–cell contacts.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a description of the software developed.

claim: Junction Mapper identifies contacting interfaces and corners with minimal user input.
source: It identifies contacting interfaces and corners with minimal user input and quantifies length, area and intensity of junction markers.
evidence: Stated in the abstract as a capability of the software.

claim: Junction Mapper's ability to measure fragmented junctions is unique.
source: Its ability to measure fragmented junctions is unique.
evidence: Explicitly stated in the abstract as a distinguishing feature.

claim: Junction Mapper can successfully quantify junctions that considerably deviate from the contiguous staining and straight contact phenotype seen in epithelia.
source: Importantly, junctions that considerably deviate from the contiguous staining and straight contact phenotype seen in epithelia are also successfully quantified (i.e. cardiomyocytes or endothelia).
evidence: Stated in the abstract with examples of cell types.

claim: Distinct phenotypes of junction disruption can be clearly differentiated among various oncogenes, depletion of actin regulators or stimulation with other agents using Junction Mapper.
source: Distinct phenotypes of junction disruption can be clearly differentiated among various oncogenes, depletion of actin regulators or stimulation with other agents.
evidence: Stated in the abstract as a capability demonstrated in the study.

claim: In epithelial tissues, the characteristic cell–cell adhesion site appears as a straight and tense or stiff junction, represented by an apparent contiguous, adjoining staining of E-cadherin receptors.
source: In epithelial tissues, the characteristic cell–cell adhesion site appears as a straight and tense or stiff junction, represented by an apparent contiguous, adjoining staining of E-cadherin receptors (the epithelia-specific cadherin protein).
evidence: Stated in the introduction as established knowledge about epithelial junctions.

claim: Growth factor treatment or oncogene expression in epithelial cells causes disturbances in the configuration of the contacting interface between cells.
source: Following stimuli such as growth factor treatment or oncogene expression in epithelial cells, the dynamic nature of cell–cell contacts is manifested in a variety of ways: disturbances in the configuration of the contacting interface between cells, fragmentation of cadherin staining or thinning out of the distribution of receptors from contacting cell borders (Braga et al., 2000; Erasmus et al., 2016; Frasa et al., 2010; Lozano et al., 2008; Nola et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to prior work.

claim: Intercalated discs in cardiomyocytes sustain considerable mechanical stress with heart beating.
source: Intercalated discs, specialised junctions in cardiomyocytes, sustain considerable mechanical stress with heart beating (Ehler, 2016; Vermij et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Extensive remodelling of the intercalated discs composition and architecture is observed in cardiac aging.
source: Extensive remodelling of the intercalated discs composition (Estigoy et al., 2009) and architecture is observed in cardiac `aging (Sessions and Engler, 2016; Tribulova et al., 2015), diabetes-induced cardiopathies (Adeghate and Singh, 2014), arrythmogenic cardiomyopathies (Calore et al., 2015) and cardiac hypertrophy and failure (Lyon et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Upon stimulation with inflammatory agonists, endothelial contacts undergo adjustments to increase permeability, changing from a linear to a zig-zag configuration.
source: Upon stimulation with inflammatory agonists (Radeva and Waschke, 2018), endothelial contacts undergo adjustments to increase permeability, changing from a linear to a zig-zag configuration and the appearance of gaps between cells (Malinova and Huveneers, 2018).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Distinct patterns of junctions are stimulus-dependent and reflect the specific destabilization or strengthening of cadherin receptors at contact sites in various cell types.
source: Collectively, the above data demonstrate that distinct patterns of junctions are stimulus-dependent and reflect the specific destabilization (or strengthening) of cadherin receptors at contact sites in various cell types.
evidence: This is a synthesis statement based on the cited literature discussed in the introduction.

claim: A major road block to furthering mechanistic studies on junction regulation is the restricted capability and efficiency of the quantitative image analysis currently available.
source: A major road block to furthering mechanistic studies on junction regulation is the restricted capability and efficiency of the quantitative image analysis currently available.
evidence: Stated as a problem motivating the development of Junction Mapper.

claim: For mammalian epithelial cells, available systems are not always suitable for the precise delineation of cell borders.
source: In contrast, for mammalian epithelial cells, available systems are not always suitable for the precise delineation of cell borders and the output of current pipelines is mostly morphometric parameters (i.e. cell size, shape, number or texture) (Campbell et al., 2017; McQuin et al., 2018; Yin et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Cell–cell borders of mammalian cells are particularly difficult to detect because of cytoplasmic noise, irregular shapes and variable junction phenotypes.
source: Cell–cell borders of mammalian cells are particularly difficult to detect because of cytoplasmic noise, irregular shapes (Held et al., 2011) and variable junction phenotypes, particularly when junctions are severely disrupted.
evidence: Supported by citation and reasoning about technical challenges.

claim: Available methodology does not enable quantification of distinct patterns of organization of receptors or junction morphometry that are readily identified by the human eye.
source: Notwithstanding these successful studies, available methodology does not enable quantification of distinct patterns of organization of receptors or junction morphometry that are readily identified by the human eye.
evidence: Stated as a limitation of existing methods.

claim: Manual methods available for junction quantification rely on intensity levels and thresholding, which are not appropriate to detect junction attributes such as alterations in shape, length, fragmentation or continuity of cell–cell contacts.
source: In addition, manual methods available for junction quantification rely on intensity levels and thresholding, which are not appropriate to detect junction attributes such as alterations in shape, length, fragmentation or continuity of cell–cell contacts.
evidence: Stated as a limitation of existing methods.

claim: The switch between a straight to undulated cell–cell contact occurs without apparent changes in receptors levels at contact sites.
source: For example, the switch between a straight to undulated cell–cell contact occurs without apparent changes in receptors levels at contact sites (Otani et al., 2006).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Junction Mapper can efficiently identify cell boundaries and cell–cell corners.
source: To address the above issues, we developed a semi-automated pipeline, Junction Mapper, which can fully capture the distinct patterns of junction perturbation by diverse stimuli in various cell types. It can efficiently (i) identify cell boundaries and cell–cell corners, (ii) describe phenotypes of junction architecture and (iii) quantify parameters that reflect the distribution and organization of junctional markers along the contacting interface.
evidence: Stated as a capability of the developed software.

claim: Junction Mapper can describe phenotypes of junction architecture.
source: To address the above issues, we developed a semi-automated pipeline, Junction Mapper, which can fully capture the distinct patterns of junction perturbation by diverse stimuli in various cell types. It can efficiently (i) identify cell boundaries and cell–cell corners, (ii) describe phenotypes of junction architecture and (iii) quantify parameters that reflect the distribution and organization of junctional markers along the contacting interface.
evidence: Stated as a capability of the developed software.

claim: Junction Mapper can quantify parameters that reflect the distribution and organization of junctional markers along the contacting interface.
source: To address the above issues, we developed a semi-automated pipeline, Junction Mapper, which can fully capture the distinct patterns of junction perturbation by diverse stimuli in various cell types. It can efficiently (i) identify cell boundaries and cell–cell corners, (ii) describe phenotypes of junction architecture and (iii) quantify parameters that reflect the distribution and organization of junctional markers along the contacting interface.
evidence: Stated as a capability of the developed software.

claim: The repertoire of parameters in Junction Mapper distinguishes subtle differences of junction disruption and provides a fingerprint for each stimulus.
source: The repertoire of parameters distinguishes subtle differences of junction disruption and provides a fingerprint for each stimulus, with insights into modes of action and how efficient and functional junctions are.
evidence: Stated as a capability demonstrated in the study.

claim: In normal epithelia, a junction between neighbouring cells usually appears as a straight, taut line, with E-cadherin receptors uniformly distributed along the contacting interface.
source: In normal epithelia, a junction between neighbouring cells usually appears as a straight, taut line, with E-cadherin receptors uniformly distributed along the contacting interface (Figure 1A).
evidence: Stated in the results section and supported by Figure 1A.

claim: Junctions are delimited by corners between three or more cells, where a specialised type of contacts are formed (tricellular junctions).
source: Junctions are delimited by corners between three or more cells, where a specialised type of contacts are formed (tricellular junctions) (Figure 1A).
evidence: Stated in the results section and supported by Figure 1A.

claim: Distinct stimuli disrupt junction architecture in different ways, from minor reduction in levels to complete removal of adhesion receptors from contacting cells.
source: Distinct stimuli disrupt the above junction architecture in different ways, from minor reduction in levels to complete removal of adhesion receptors from contacting cells (Figure 1B).
evidence: Stated in the results section and supported by Figure 1B.

claim: Concomitant with changes in levels, junction configuration and architecture are also compromised, which are not always captured by intensity measurements.
source: Concomitant with changes in levels, junction configuration and architecture are also compromised, which are not always captured by intensity measurements.
evidence: Stated as an observation motivating the need for new parameters.

claim: Junction Mapper builds from quantitative analysis of images from RNAi screens.
source: We designed and validated a semi-automated system (Figure 2), Junction Mapper, that builds from our quantitative analysis of images from RNAi screens (Erasmus et al., 2016).
evidence: Stated with citation to prior work.

claim: Junction Mapper implements novel quantification tools including corners, length and area.
source: Junction Mapper implements novel quantification tools (corners, length and area) and a variety of novel primary and secondary parameters expressed per individual junction.
evidence: Stated as a feature of the software.

claim: The main advantage of Junction Mapper is to efficiently segment junctions in a variety of cell types and of different junction patterns, from linear to fragmented or disrupted contacts.
source: The main advantage of Junction Mapper is to efficiently segment junctions in a variety of cell types and of different junction patterns, from linear to fragmented or disrupted contacts.
evidence: Stated as the main advantage of the software.

claim: The software detects the contacting interface between two cells and obtains a skeletonized edge map.
source: The software detects the contacting interface between two cells and obtains a skeletonized edge map (summarised stepwise in Figure 2—figure supplement 1; see Materials and methods).
evidence: Stated as a capability and referenced to supplementary figure.

claim: Users can adjust the outline manually by removing incorrect or adding missing lines, with subsequent refinement of the line location and geometry by the software algorithm.
source: Although semi-automated, users can adjust the outline manually by removing incorrect or adding missing lines, with subsequent refinement of the line location and geometry by the software algorithm (detailed in Appendix 1).
evidence: Stated as a feature of the software.

claim: A dilation step is applied to define the area to be quantified around the skeletonized map.
source: A dilation step is applied (user controlled) to define the area to be quantified around the skeletonized map (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Stated as a step in the software workflow.

claim: The software automatically identifies each cell–cell corner.
source: To identify individual junctions for further quantification, the software then automatically identifies each cell–cell corner (i.e. point of contact between three or more cells, see its mathematical definition in Appendix 1).
evidence: Stated as a capability of the software.

claim: The number and location of corners in each cell can be manually adjusted by the user.
source: The number and location of corners in each cell can also be manually adjusted by the user (Appendix 1).
evidence: Stated as a feature of the software.

claim: Images obtained at different resolutions can be used for analyses in Junction Mapper.
source: Images obtained at different resolutions can be used for analyses in Junction Mapper (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: Stated as a capability with reference to supplementary file.

claim: For defining the automated skeletonized edge of each image, a suitable signal-to-noise ratio is necessary to ensure enough contrast to differentiate staining at junctions from the cytoplasm.
source: For defining the automated skeletonized edge of each image, a suitable signal-to-noise ratio is necessary to ensure enough contrast to differentiate staining at junctions from the cytoplasm (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Stated as a requirement and supported by figure.

claim: For efficient skeleton definition the Peak Signal to Noise ratio should be above 22 dB.
source: For efficient skeleton definition the ratio should be above 22 dB (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Stated as a threshold value and supported by figure.

claim: The higher the fragmentation of junctions in the image, the more user input is necessary to define the final skeleton outline for quantification.
source: The higher the fragmentation of junctions in the image, the more user input is necessary to define the final skeleton outline for quantification.
evidence: Stated as an observation about software usage.

claim: The measurement of the different parameters is performed simultaneously and automatically, in an unbiased manner.
source: The measurement of the different parameters is performed simultaneously and automatically, in an unbiased manner (Figure 2).
evidence: Stated as a feature of the software.

claim: The output per junction is produced as an Excel file that contains the selected image, skeleton and the quantification of pre-designed measurements and parameters.
source: The output per junction is produced as an Excel file that contains the selected image, skeleton and the quantification of pre-designed measurements and parameters (see below).
evidence: Stated as a feature of the software output.

claim: Different phenotypes of junction perturbation may require a distinct set of parameters to appropriately capture the disruption features.
source: We envisage that different phenotypes of junction perturbation may require a distinct set of parameters to appropriately capture the disruption features (Figure 1).
evidence: Stated as a rationale for the parameter design.

claim: Interface is the contacting membrane between two neighbouring cells and delimited by cell–cell corners.
source: Interface is the contacting membrane between two neighbouring cells and delimited by cell–cell corners.
evidence: Stated as a definition used in the study.

claim: A cell–cell contact or junction is the region of the interface covered by adhesion receptors.
source: A cell–cell contact or junction is the region of the interface covered by adhesion receptors (e.g. cadherin staining).
evidence: Stated as a definition used in the study.

claim: Junctions may or may not extend to the whole of the interface (corner-to-corner), and can appear fragmented or dotted.
source: Junctions may or may not extend to the whole of the interface (corner-to-corner), and can appear fragmented or dotted (Figure 1, Figure 3A).
evidence: Stated as an observation and supported by figures.

claim: Area is the dilated region around the skeleton and is set to encompass the width of a junctional marker staining.
source: Area is the dilated region around the skeleton and is set to encompass the width of a junctional marker staining (which can vary in thickness).
evidence: Stated as a definition used in the study.

claim: Contour is the length measurement of the outline of the skeleton between defined points (interface or junction).
source: Contour is the length measurement of the outline of the skeleton between defined points (interface or junction).
evidence: Stated as a definition used in the study.

claim: The straight-line length is defined as the shortest distance (Euclidian distance) between corners that form the boundaries of one junction or interface.
source: Finally, the straight-line length is defined as the shortest distance (Euclidian distance) between corners that form the boundaries of one junction or interface.
evidence: Stated as a definition used in the study.

claim: The primary parameters were validated to assess measurements were as predicted from their definition.
source: The primary parameters were validated to assess measurements were as predicted from their definition.
evidence: Stated as a validation approach.

claim: Junction contour and area were more severely disrupted when two neighbouring cells contained exogenous H-RasG12V.
source: Measurements of the primary parameters (Figure 3) confirmed that junction contour and area were more severely disrupted when two neighbouring cells contained exogenous H-RasG12V (Figure 4D–E).
evidence: Stated as a result and supported by figures.

claim: The interface of mosaic contacts shared by expressing and non-expressing cells (en) were not significantly different from controls.
source: The interface of mosaic contacts shared by expressing and non-expressing cells (en) were not significantly different from controls (Figure 4B,C,F).
evidence: Stated as a result and supported by figures.

claim: Increasing the dilation values modifies the area-based but not the length-based measurements.
source: Increasing the dilation values modifies the area-based (D) but not the length-based measurements (C).
evidence: Stated as a result from validation experiments.

claim: Larger dilation values obtained higher VE-cadherin area measurements at the undulated contacts.
source: Larger dilation values obtained higher VE-cadherin area measurements at the undulated contacts (H).
evidence: Stated as a result from validation experiments.

claim: Increasing thresholding levels did not interfere with interface contour length, as it is defined by the position of corners.
source: Increasing thresholding levels did not interfere with interface contour length, as it is defined by the position of corners (C).
evidence: Stated as a result from validation experiments.

claim: The fragmented junction length was reduced by increasing thresholding.
source: The fragmented junction length was reduced by increasing thresholding (C), similar to what was observed with the E-cadherin area and intensity (D).
evidence: Stated as a result from validation experiments.

claim: The primary parameters measure the length and area of various features as predicted and are selectively modulated by user-controlled settings in accordance to their definition.
source: Taken together, we concluded that the primary parameters measure the length and area of various features as predicted and are selectively modulated by user-controlled settings in accordance to their definition (Appendix 1).
evidence: Stated as a conclusion from validation experiments.

claim: The Linearity Index measures how straight an interface between two cells is.
source: The Linearity Index measures how straight an interface between two cells is, as proposed by Takeichi and colleagues (Otani et al., 2006).
evidence: Stated as a parameter definition with citation.

claim: Coverage Index is a length measurement of the percentage of the interface length that is covered by the junction marker staining.
source: Coverage Index is a length measurement of the percentage of the interface length that is covered by the junction marker staining and has been previously used manually in the lab (Lozano et al., 2008).
evidence: Stated as a parameter definition with citation.

claim: Interface Occupancy measures the area occupied by the marker within the Interface Area of each junction.
source: First, Interface Occupancy, measures the area occupied by the marker within the Interface Area of each junction.
evidence: Stated as a parameter definition.

claim: Junction Protein Intensity per Interface area calculates the fluorescence intensity within the Interface Area.
source: Second, Junction Protein Intensity per Interface area calculates the fluorescence intensity within the Interface Area.
evidence: Stated as a parameter definition.

claim: Cluster Density is the junction protein intensity level within the area delimited by its staining.
source: Finally, Cluster Density is the junction protein intensity level within the area delimited by its staining (i.e. Fragmented Junction Area, which considers any fragmentation of the staining; additional parameters are described in Appendix 2).
evidence: Stated as a parameter definition.

claim: The Coverage Index parameter calculated by Junction Mapper was validated by manual quantification using FIJI on cells expressing active Rac1.
source: The Coverage Index parameter calculated by Junction Mapper was validated by manual quantification using FIJI on cells expressing active Rac1 (Supplementary file 2A-B).
evidence: Stated as a validation approach.

claim: Using either quantification, manual or Junction Mapper, a significant statistical difference was observed between values of control and Rac1-expressing cells.
source: Using either quantification, manual or Junction Mapper, a significant statistical difference was observed between values of control and Rac1-expressing cells (Supplementary file 2C).
evidence: Stated as a result from validation experiments.

claim: Lower values were obtained with the manual quantification method as predicted when using straight-lines for measurement.
source: Lower values were obtained with the manual quantification method as predicted when using straight-lines for measurement.
evidence: Stated as a result from validation experiments.

claim: When controls values were compared between the two methods, no statistical difference was obtained.
source: However, when controls values were compared between the two methods, no statistical difference was obtained (Supplementary file 2C).
evidence: Stated as a result from validation experiments.

claim: The reproducibility of secondary parameters was assessed in independent biological replicates by the same user.
source: Thus, the parameters give results as expected from previous manual methods. In addition, the reproducibility of secondary parameters was assessed in independent biological replicates by the same user.
evidence: Stated as a validation approach.

claim: Across biological replicates of cells overexpressing active Rac1, the absolute values obtained for each sample were slightly different.
source: Across biological replicates of cells overexpressing active Rac1, the absolute values obtained for each sample were slightly different (Scheme 1B-D).
evidence: Stated as a result and supported by scheme.

claim: The overall result is the same between replicates: a reduction of Coverage Index and Interface Occupancy of E-cadherin at junctions from Rac1 expressing cells.
source: However, the overall result is the same between replicates: a reduction of Coverage Index and Interface Occupancy of E-cadherin at junctions from Rac1 expressing cells (Scheme 1B-D).
evidence: Stated as a result and supported by scheme.

claim: Comparison of control values between biological replicates (or between Rac1 expressing cells) was not statistically different.
source: Comparison of control values between biological replicates (or between Rac1 expressing cells) was not statistically different.
evidence: Stated as a result from validation experiments.

claim: Confluent epithelial monolayers with clearly defined junctions and corners produced less output variability from different users than images with disrupted contacts.
source: Confluent epithelial monolayers with clearly defined junctions and corners produced less output variability from different users than images with disrupted contacts (Supplementary file 3A-D).
evidence: Stated as a result from user-bias validation.

claim: A particular hot spot for differences was the identification of cell corners in disrupted contacts, where corners are often not covered by cadherin staining.
source: We found that a particular hot spot for differences was the identification of cell corners in disrupted contacts, where corners are often not covered by cadherin staining (Supplementary file 3B).
evidence: Stated as a result from user-bias validation.

claim: Pair-wise comparison of primary parameters of matched epithelial junctions obtained independently by two users showed significant differences.
source: Second, pair-wise comparison of primary parameters of matched epithelial junctions obtained independently by two users showed significant differences (Supplementary file 3C-D).
evidence: Stated as a result from user-bias validation.

claim: When secondary parameters were calculated, the profiles obtained by the two users were similar, aside the absolute values being different.
source: However, when secondary parameters were calculated, the profiles obtained by the two users were similar, aside the absolute values being different (Supplementary file 3E-F, see also Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Stated as a result from user-bias validation.

claim: User bias can be minimized by using secondary parameters and normalizing to controls in each replicate.
source: We conclude that, in addition to the impact of dilation and thresholding settings, Junction Mapper results are impacted by user influence on the cell edge map. This influence is stronger in cell images with disrupted cell–cell contacts, where higher frequency of inaccurate corner and skeleton detection occurs. Hence more manual edge correction is required the more robust secondary parameter measurements should be considered. Furthermore, absolute comparisons can not be made between experiments. Instead, normalization of secondary parameters to controls in each replicate will facilitate comparisons.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion from user-bias validation.

claim: Junction perturbation occurs more efficiently between two RacQ61L-expressing neighbouring keratinocytes.
source: Previous visual analysis indicated that perturbation of cell–cell contacts occurs more efficiently between two RacQ61L-expressing neighbouring keratinocytes (Braga et al., 1997; Lozano et al., 2008).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Oncogenic H-Ras expression induces a longer contacting interface between cells and a progressive fragmentation of E-cadherin staining.
source: Based on the quantification of the primary parameters, oncogenic H-Ras expression induces a longer contacting interface between cells and a progressive fragmentation of E-cadherin staining.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion from the data analysis.

claim: Active Src expression did not promote elongation of the contacting interface or an increase in interface area.
source: For example, active Src expression did not promote elongation of the contacting interface or an increase in interface area (Figure 4—figure supplement 1H–I), while active Rac1 did not induce fragmentation of cadherin staining (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D–E).
evidence: Stated as a result and supported by figures.

claim: Active Rac1 did not induce fragmentation of cadherin staining.
source: For example, active Src expression did not promote elongation of the contacting interface or an increase in interface area (Figure 4—figure supplement 1H–I), while active Rac1 did not induce fragmentation of cadherin staining (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D–E).
evidence: Stated as a result and supported by figures.

claim: Distinct subsets of parameters can differentiate alterations by different stimuli, thereby providing a unique disruption profile.
source: The above data may indicate that distinct subsets of parameters can differentiate alterations by different stimuli, thereby providing a unique disruption profile (Figure 5).
evidence: Stated as an interpretation of the results.

claim: The undulation of the interface was increased among cells expressing H-RasG12V or SrcY527F when compared to controls.
source: When compared to controls, the undulation of the interface was increased among cells expressing H-RasG12V or SrcY527F (higher Interface Linearity Index, Figure 5B,D), but remained unchanged for Rac1Q61L-perturbed junctions (ee, Figure 5F).
evidence: Stated as a result and supported by figures.

claim: The undulation of the interface remained unchanged for Rac1Q61L-perturbed junctions.
source: When compared to controls, the undulation of the interface was increased among cells expressing H-RasG12V or SrcY527F (higher Interface Linearity Index, Figure 5B,D), but remained unchanged for Rac1Q61L-perturbed junctions (ee, Figure 5F).
evidence: Stated as a result and supported by figures.

claim: As E-cadherin is removed from junctions, the interface between H-RasG12V and SrcY527F expressing cells becomes less tensile.
source: These data indicate that, as E-cadherin is removed from junctions, the interface between H-RasG12V and SrcY527F expressing cells becomes less tensile.
evidence: Stated as an interpretation of the results.

claim: The percentage of the interface area occupied by E-cadherin receptors was decreased in all samples expressing activated oncogenes.
source: The percentage of the interface area occupied by E-cadherin receptors was decreased in all samples (Interface Occupancy, Figure 5B,F), but did not reach significance in Src-expressing cells (Figure 5D).
evidence: Stated as a result and supported by figures.

claim: The intensity levels of cadherin at junctions was significantly reduced following transfection of activated H-Ras or Src.
source: The intensity levels of cadherin at junctions was significantly reduced following transfection of activated H-Ras or Src when measured as raw values (E-cadherin Intensity) or corrected per contacting area between two cells (E-cadherin Intensity per Interface Area) (Figure 5B,D).
evidence: Stated as a result and supported by figures.

claim: After active Rac1 expression, neither E-cadherin Intensity nor E-cadherin Intensity per Interface Area was significantly changed.
source: In contrast, after active Rac1 expression, neither parameter was significantly changed.
evidence: Stated as a result.

claim: The density of cadherin clusters was decreased in H-RasG12V and SrcY527F, but slightly augmented in RacQ61L.
source: Consistent with the distinct phenotype of junction perturbation seen in Rac1Q61L-transfected cells, the density of cadherin clusters was decreased in H-RasG12V and SrcY527F, but slightly augmented in RacQ61L.
evidence: Stated as a result.

claim: Activated Rac1 does not significantly reduce the overall levels of E-cadherin at junctions.
source: Our preliminary observations suggest that activated Rac1 does not significantly reduce the overall levels of E-cadherin at junctions, since receptor intensity at the interface area is not reduced.
evidence: Stated as an interpretation of the results.

claim: Rac1 activation progressively redistributes receptors at the junction, maintaining straight, linear junctions.
source: Rather, Rac1 activation progressively redistributes receptors at the junction (reduced Interface Occupancy and higher Cluster Density), maintaining straight, linear junctions.
evidence: Stated as an interpretation of the results.

claim: Activated H-Ras or Src disrupt junctions via fragmentation and removal of E-cadherin consistently throughout the contacting interface.
source: In contrast, activated H-Ras or Src disrupt junctions via fragmentation and removal of E-cadherin consistently throughout the contacting interface (decreased in Interface Occupancy and Cluster Density), with concomitant undulation of cell–cell contacts (i.e. reduced tension or stiffness at junctions).
evidence: Stated as an interpretation of the results.

claim: Depletion of CIP4 results in modest, but significant fluctuations in E-cadherin at junctions (20%–30%).
source: Depletion of CIP4 (a regulator of cadherin trafficking) (Leibfried et al., 2008; Rolland et al., 2014), VAV2 (an exchange factor for Rho, Rac2 and Cdc42) (Vigil et al., 2010) or EEF1A (an actin bundling protein) (Mateyak and Kinzy, 2010) results in modest, but significant fluctuations in E-cadherin at junctions (20%–30%) using a thresholding method (Erasmus et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior work.

claim: CIP4, VAV2 or EEF1A siRNA did not interfere with the linearity of the contacting interface.
source: When analysed with Junction Mapper, CIP4, VAV2 or EEF1A siRNA did not interfere with the linearity of the contacting interface (Figure 6B,D,F), in line with the appearance of normal, linear junctions.
evidence: Stated as a result and supported by figures.

claim: A small decrease in E-cadherin intensity was observed in both CIP4- and VAV2-depleted cells.
source: Consistent with our previous findings (Erasmus et al., 2016), a small decrease in E-cadherin intensity was observed in both CIP4- and VAV2-depleted cells (Figure 6B,F), while EEF1A siRNA promoted the unusual phenotype of higher levels of cadherin receptors (Figure 6D).
evidence: Stated as a result and supported by figures and citation.

claim: EEF1A siRNA promoted the unusual phenotype of higher levels of cadherin receptors.
source: Consistent with our previous findings (Erasmus et al., 2016), a small decrease in E-cadherin intensity was observed in both CIP4- and VAV2-depleted cells (Figure 6B,F), while EEF1A siRNA promoted the unusual phenotype of higher levels of cadherin receptors (Figure 6D).
evidence: Stated as a result and supported by figures.

claim: Despite the similar reduction in E-cadherin intensity levels following VAV2 and CIP4 depletion, receptors were removed in different ways from junctions.
source: Strikingly, despite the similar reduction in E-cadherin intensity levels following VAV2 and CIP4 depletion, receptors were removed in different ways from junctions.
evidence: Stated as a result.

claim: The clusters of cadherin receptors were less dense with lower levels of CIP4.
source: The clusters of cadherin receptors were less dense with lower levels of CIP4, while upon VAV2 siRNA, the density of the clusters slightly increased (Cluster density, Figure 6B,F).
evidence: Stated as a result and supported by figures.

claim: Upon VAV2 siRNA, the density of the cadherin clusters slightly increased.
source: The clusters of cadherin receptors were less dense with lower levels of CIP4, while upon VAV2 siRNA, the density of the clusters slightly increased (Cluster density, Figure 6B,F).
evidence: Stated as a result and supported by figures.

claim: The discrete changes in junctions result from reduced cadherin levels throughout the contacting interface by lower density of receptor clusters (CIP4 RNAi) or localised E-cadherin removal and redistribution into denser clusters (VAV2 RNAi).
source: Thus, the discrete changes in junctions result from reduced cadherin levels throughout the contacting interface by lower density of receptor clusters (CIP4 RNAi) or localised E-cadherin removal and redistribution into denser clusters (VAV2 RNAi; Figure 6B,F).
evidence: Stated as an interpretation of the results.

claim: EEF1A depletion augmented E-cadherin Intensity and Cluster Density along the interface.
source: In contrast, EEF1A depletion augmented E-cadherin Intensity and Cluster Density along the interface.
evidence: Stated as a result.

claim: Junction Mapper can detect phenotypes reproducibly and with good dynamic range.
source: Taken together, these data highlight the ability of the Junction Mapper to detect phenotypes reproducibly and with good dynamic range.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion from the data analysis.

claim: Thrombin is a serine protease that stimulates protease-activated receptor (PAR) in endothelial cells to increase vascular permeability in inflammation and injury.
source: Thrombin is a serine protease that stimulates protease-activated receptor (PAR) in endothelial cells to increase vascular permeability in inflammation and injury (Figure 7A) (Kumar et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior work.

claim: There were no significant changes in the Interface Linearity Index in thrombin-treated endothelial cells.
source: There were no significant changes in the Interface Linearity Index (Figure 7A,B), consistent with the limitation of Junction Mapper to skeletonize zig-zagged junctions and thus measure their length (Figure 3—figure supplement 2E–F).
evidence: Stated as a result and supported by figures.

claim: In thrombin-treated cells, VE-cadherin distribution along the interface area (Interface Occupancy), intensity of VE-cadherin staining and normalised intensity per contacting interface were substantially higher.
source: However, with appropriate dilation values (Supplementary file 1, Figure 3—figure supplement 1), alterations were detected for area-based measurements. In thrombin-treated cells, VE-cadherin distribution along the interface area (Interface Occupancy), intensity of VE-cadherin staining and normalised intensity per contacting interface were substantially higher (Figure 7C–E).
evidence: Stated as a result and supported by figures.

claim: The density of VE-cadherin clusters was enhanced upon treatment with thrombin.
source: The density of VE-cadherin clusters was also enhanced upon treatment with thrombin (Figure 7F), implying that a higher number of receptors is recruited per contact area.
evidence: Stated as a result and supported by figures.

claim: The increased levels of VE-cadherin at junctions may promote stronger endothelial adhesion, which is relevant to sustain elevated intracellular tension and contractility induced by thrombin stimulation.
source: Using area-based parameters, we find that the contacting interface is occupied more efficiently, with higher density of VE-cadherin receptors at endothelial junctions upon thrombin treatment. Thus, it seems that the increased levels of VE-cadherin at junctions may promote stronger endothelial adhesion, which is relevant to sustain elevated intracellular tension and contractility induced by thrombin stimulation.
evidence: Stated as an interpretation of the results.

claim: These results are consistent with the role of mechanical tension in receptor modulation and integrity of multicellular tissues.
source: These results are consistent with the role of mechanical tension in receptor modulation and integrity of multicellular tissues (Liu et al., 2010), and merit further experimentation.
evidence: Supported by citation to prior work.

claim: At steady state, in control cardiomyocytes, intercalated discs have clusters of cadherin receptors that are far apart.
source: At steady state, our data show that, in control cardiomyocytes, intercalated discs have clusters of cadherin receptors that are far apart.
evidence: Stated as a result.

claim: Hypertrophic stimulus in cellulo (neonatal rat cardiomyocytes) potently increases the levels of β-catenin at contacting interfaces.
source: Hypertrophic stimulus in cellulo (neonatal rat cardiomyocytes) potently increases the levels of β-catenin at contacting interfaces, consistent with what was reported in hamster and human hypertrophic hearts (Masuelli et al., 2003).
evidence: Stated as a result and supported by citation.

claim: Connexin 43 total protein and mRNA levels are augmented by hypertrophic signals in cellulo.
source: Connexin 43 is a major connexin isoform found in cardiomyocytes and its total protein and mRNA levels are augmented by hypertrophic signals in cellulo (i.e. phenylephrine) (Salameh et al., 2008; Stanbouly et al., 2008) or in human hearts with compensated left-ventricular hypertrophy by pressure-overloading (Kostin et al., 2004).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The formation of gap junctions is enhanced after hypertrophy stimulation in cellulo.
source: The initial profiling analysis with Junction Mapper suggest that the formation of gap junctions is enhanced after hypertrophy stimulation in cellulo, confirming the broadening of intercalated disc area and higher number of GAP junctions in compensated hypertrophic hearts of human patients (Kostin et al., 2004).
evidence: Stated as a result and supported by citation.

claim: Although hypertrophic stimulus increases both β-catenin and connexin 43 levels at intercalated discs, these markers are regulated in distinct ways.
source: Although hypertrophic stimulus increases both β-catenin and connexin 43 levels at intercalated discs, these markers are regulated in distinct ways.
evidence: Stated as a result.

claim: The β-catenin cluster density is decreased leading to a more contiguous distribution after hypertrophic stimulus.
source: The β-catenin cluster density is decreased leading to a more contiguous distribution, while connexin 43 is localised in clusters of higher density.
evidence: Stated as a result.

claim: Connexin 43 is localised in clusters of higher density after hypertrophic stimulus.
source: The β-catenin cluster density is decreased leading to a more contiguous distribution, while connexin 43 is localised in clusters of higher density.
evidence: Stated as a result.

claim: The most innovative aspects of Junction Mapper are the measurement of receptor density and occupancy, the automatic quantification of fragmented staining at a junction, and the correlation of the parameters from two junctional markers along the same junction.
source: The most innovative aspects of Junction Mapper are, first, the measurement of receptor density and occupancy, via the normalization of the junction marker intensity, length and area to the available contacting interface and cell–cell contact area. Second, the automatic quantification of fragmented staining at a junction, which has not been feasible previously and, third, the correlation of the parameters from two junctional markers along the same junction.
evidence: Stated as the innovative aspects of the software.

claim: Machine learning algorithms have the potential to improve and automate segmentation success, especially of highly fragmented contacts.
source: Machine learning algorithms certainly have the potential to improve and automate segmentation success, especially of highly fragmented contacts.
evidence: Stated as a future direction.

claim: The availability of training image datasets with boundaries manually-generated is still a bottleneck for machine learning algorithms.
source: However, the availability of training image datasets with boundaries manually-generated is still a bottleneck (Häring et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation.

claim: One possible use of the software is the generation of precise cell outline skeletons that can be used to train machine-learning algorithms in the future.
source: One possible use of the software is therefore the generation of precise cell outline skeletons that can be used to train machine-learning algorithms in the future.
evidence: Stated as a potential application.

claim: User contribution is necessary and essential to perform the quality control of skeleton outline, corner positioning and setting up the dilation and threshold levels in a given dataset.
source: While semi-automation has been implemented during the image processing by Junction Mapper, user contribution is necessary and essential to perform the quality control of skeleton outline, corner positioning and setting up the dilation and threshold levels in a given dataset.
evidence: Stated as a requirement of the software.

claim: User bias is particularly relevant in images with very disrupted and irregular junctions.
source: User bias is particularly relevant in images with very disrupted and irregular junctions, and absolute values are not suitable for comparison across experiments in some cases.
evidence: Stated as a limitation.

claim: Analysis of biological replicates or independent analysis by different users show that the secondary parameters are more robust against user bias.
source: However, user bias can be minimized. Analysis of biological replicates or independent analysis by different users show that (i) the secondary parameters are more robust against user bias and (ii) obtained results are similar across replicates when comparing control and treated samples.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion from validation experiments.

claim: The software can detect both major and minor changes at junctions in different experiments.
source: The software can detect both major and minor changes at junctions in different experiments.
evidence: Stated as a capability of the software.

claim: Unexpected and distinct profiles emerge from junction disruption by oncogenes that potently remove E-cadherin from contacts.
source: Unexpected and distinct profiles emerge from junction disruption by oncogenes that potently remove E-cadherin from contacts.
evidence: Stated as a result.

claim: Among the repertoire of pre-defined parameters, a subset is highly likely to assess the features of a particular junction phenotype.
source: Among the repertoire of pre-defined parameters, we find that a subset is highly likely to assess the features of a particular junction phenotype.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion.

claim: Junction Mapper analysis confirms mild phenotypes previously observed with manual, threshold-based quantifications of whole images.
source: Junction Mapper analysis confirms mild phenotypes previously observed with manual, threshold-based quantifications of whole images (Erasmus et al., 2016), that indicate either an increase (EEF1A siRNA) or a decrease (CIP4 or VAV2 siRNA) in the intensity levels of E-cadherin.
evidence: Stated as a result and supported by citation.

claim: The profiling with new parameters underscores the potential of Junction Mapper to differentiate among distinct, subtle modes of junction perturbation.
source: The profiling with new parameters underscores the potential of Junction Mapper to differentiate among distinct, subtle modes of junction perturbation.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion.

claim: The remarkable zig-zag pattern of thrombin-stimulated endothelial junctions correlates with increased vascular permeability.
source: The remarkable zig-zag pattern of thrombin-stimulated endothelial junctions correlates with increased vascular permeability (Malinova and Huveneers, 2018) but it is not recognized by the automated skeleton definition.
evidence: Supported by citation.

claim: The zig-zag pattern of thrombin-stimulated endothelial junctions is not recognized by the automated skeleton definition.
source: The remarkable zig-zag pattern of thrombin-stimulated endothelial junctions correlates with increased vascular permeability (Malinova and Huveneers, 2018) but it is not recognized by the automated skeleton definition.
evidence: Stated as a limitation.

claim: In control cardiomyocytes, intercalated discs have clusters of cadherin receptors that are far apart.
source: Because of the fragmented and undulated nature of cardiomyocyte contacts (Ehler, 2016; Vermij et al., 2017), quantitative imaging tools specifically designed for intercalated discs have not been available or systematically used. At steady state, our data show that, in control cardiomyocytes, intercalated discs have clusters of cadherin receptors that are far apart.
evidence: Stated as a result and supported by citations.

claim: Hypertrophic stimulus in cellulo (neonatal rat cardiomyocytes) potently increases the levels of β-catenin at contacting interfaces, consistent with what was reported in hamster and human hypertrophic hearts.
source: Hypertrophic stimulus in cellulo (neonatal rat cardiomyocytes) potently increases the levels of β-catenin at contacting interfaces, consistent with what was reported in hamster and human hypertrophic hearts (Masuelli et al., 2003).
evidence: Stated as a result and supported by citation.

claim: The initial profiling analysis with Junction Mapper suggest that the formation of gap junctions is enhanced after hypertrophy stimulation in cellulo, confirming the broadening of intercalated disc area and higher number of GAP junctions in compensated hypertrophic hearts of human patients.
source: The initial profiling analysis with Junction Mapper suggest that the formation of gap junctions is enhanced after hypertrophy stimulation in cellulo, confirming the broadening of intercalated disc area and higher number of GAP junctions in compensated hypertrophic hearts of human patients (Kostin et al., 2004).
evidence: Stated as a result and supported by citation.

claim: The quantification of very fragmented and zig-zagged junctions such as those in endothelia and cardiomyocytes is a challenge that Junction Mapper has begun to address.
source: Clearly, further investigation is necessary to ascertain the profiling and biological significance of the phenotypes observed in different models. The quantification of very fragmented and zig-zagged junctions such as those in endothelia and cardiomyocytes is a challenge that Junction Mapper has begun to address, but improvements in future computation studies are welcomed.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion and future direction.

claim: The complexity of fragmented and zig-zagged junctions requires more user input to quality control the definition of the skeleton and corners.
source: The complexity of these junctions also requires more user input to quality control the definition of the skeleton and corners.
evidence: Stated as a limitation.

claim: The ability of Junction Mapper to quantify junctions in a stratified epithelium remains to be tested.
source: In addition, the ability of Junction Mapper to quantify junctions in a stratified epithelium, where the added complexity of multiple epithelial cell layers provides an additional challenge, remains to be tested.
evidence: Stated as a limitation and future direction.

claim: The detailed fine mapping of junction properties forms a basis to distinguish between disassembly mechanisms and infer cellular processes such as intracellular trafficking, receptor clustering or modulation of contraction at junctions.
source: We foresee the potential of Junction Mapper in distinct research areas, due to its innovative and in-depth approach to quantify cell–cell contacts. The detailed fine mapping of junction properties forms a basis to distinguish between disassembly mechanisms and infer cellular processes such as intracellular trafficking, receptor clustering or modulation of contraction at junctions.
evidence: Stated as a potential application.

claim: The fingerprinting of junction phenotypes after different stimuli is a powerful tool in pathway inference and guides rescue and translational experiments.
source: As multiple cellular processes contribute to junction stability, the fingerprinting of junction phenotypes after different stimuli is a powerful tool in pathway inference and guides rescue and translational experiments.
evidence: Stated as a potential application.

claim: Junction Mapper's broad dynamic range, repertoire of novel parameters and applicability to quantify junctions in various cell types will have a significant impact on studies in numerous model systems.
source: Despite its limitations, Junction Mapper's broad dynamic range, repertoire of novel parameters and applicability to quantify junctions in various cell types will have a significant impact on studies in numerous model systems.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion about the software's impact.

claim: The generation of tools to facilitate unbiased phenotype identification will be a major step forward to understand how junction dynamics are modulated in homeostasis and pathologies of different tissues.
source: Most importantly, the generation of tools to facilitate unbiased phenotype identification will be a major step forward to understand how junction dynamics are modulated in homeostasis and pathologies of different tissues.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion about the broader impact.

claim: Junction Mapper is an open access, standalone and downloadable software developed in Java.
source: Junction Mapper is an open access, standalone and downloadable software developed in Java.
evidence: Stated in the methods section.

claim: The Junction Mapper code has been deposited in GitHub.
source: The Junction Mapper code has been deposited in GitHub (license GNU GENERAL PUBLIC LICENSE; https://github.com/ImperialCollegeLondon/Junction_Mapper; copy archived at https://github.com/elifesciences-publications/Junction_Mapper) and the software, instructions and its documentation can be downloaded from https://dataman.bioinformatics.ic.ac.uk/junction_mapper.
evidence: Stated in the methods section.

claim: The novelty of Junction Mapper lays in the integration of distinct measurements, calculations of new parameters and consolidation of all parameters in a single system.
source: The novelty of Junction Mapper lays in the integration of distinct measurements, calculations of new parameters and consolidation of all parameters in a single system.
evidence: Stated in the methods section.
